Control your **LIFX** bulbs, strips and matrices from Gladys, **on the local
network**, with the official LIFX LAN protocol: no cloud, no account, no key.

> Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome. The integration was built
> from the public LIFX protocol and tested against simulated lights. If
> something does not behave as described, please open an issue:
> https://github.com/guim31/gladys-lifx/issues

This integration is not affiliated with LIFX.

## Overview

- Every LIFX light becomes a Gladys light: on/off, brightness, color, white
  temperature (in kelvins, within the range of your model).
- **Nightvision** bulbs get their **infrared** level.
- **Strips** (Z, Beam, Neon, String, Permanent Outdoor...) and **matrices**
  (Tile, Candle, Ceiling, Spot, Path, Tube...) are controlled as a whole
  (on/off, brightness, one color for the whole light), and get the list of
  their built-in effects.
- Two scene actions: **Pulse a LIFX light** (an alert in color that ends by
  itself) and **Start a LIFX effect** (Move, Morph, Flame).
- The connection of each light is shown, and kept in the history.

## Requirements

- Gladys 5.1 or later.
- LIFX lights set up in the LIFX app and connected to the same network as
  Gladys. The LIFX app is no longer needed afterwards.
- The lights answer on UDP port 56700. Gladys finds them by a broadcast on the
  local network: if Gladys and the lights are on different networks (VLAN,
  guest Wi-Fi), enter their IP addresses in the configuration.

## Configuration

1. Install the integration (Integrations → Install from GitHub, or from the
   store).
2. Open the **Configuration** tab. Every field is optional:
   - **IP addresses of LIFX lights**: only for the lights the automatic
     discovery does not find, separated by commas. Give them a fixed address
     in your router.
   - **Refresh interval**: how often each light is read (10, 15, 30 or 60
     seconds, 15 by default), to follow the changes made from the LIFX app, a
     voice assistant or a wall switch.
   - **Transition**: a fade for the changes made from Gladys (none by default,
     up to 5 seconds).
   - **Language of the feature names**: the language of the names given to the
     features of new lights (French by default).
3. Open the **Discovery** tab and add your lights. Their names are the ones
   given in the LIFX app; you can rename them in Gladys.

The **Search for LIFX lights** button of the Configuration tab looks for the
lights again and lists the ones found, with their address and model.

## Devices and features

Each light is one Gladys device, keyed on its serial number: it keeps its
history, scenes and dashboards when its IP address changes.

| Feature               | Lights                    | What it does                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Light**             | all                       | on/off                                                           |
| **Brightness**        | all                       | 0 to 100 %; 0 turns the light off                                |
| **Color**             | color lights              | the color; never changes the brightness                          |
| **Color temperature** | lights with a white range | the white in kelvins, within the range of the model and firmware |
| **Infrared**          | Nightvision               | 0 to 100 % of the infrared power                                 |
| **LIFX effect**       | strips and matrices       | **None**, the effects of the light, **Other effect** (read only) |
| **Connection**        | all                       | 1 when the light answers, 0 when it does not (read only)         |

A color, a white or a brightness also turns the light on. A light that is off
takes its new color first, then fades on: it never flashes its old color. A
color or a white stops the running effect, which would cover it.

The color is shown while the light shows a color, the color temperature while
it shows a white. A light that no longer answers (switched off at the wall,
power cut) is shown off, with **Connection** at 0 and the "unreachable" badge.

Effects of the **LIFX effect** list: **Move** slides the colors of a strip;
**Morph** blends colors and **Flame** flickers on a matrix. From the list, they
start with their default settings; the scene action gives the choice of the
speed, the direction and the colors. An effect started from the LIFX app that
the integration does not start itself (Sky, Color sweep...) shows as **Other
effect**.

## Scene actions

### Pulse a LIFX light

The light blinks or breathes in a color, a number of times, then goes back to
what it showed. A light that is off lights up for the pulse and goes back off
after it, with its color. Made for alerts: a door left open, the washing
machine done, someone at the door.

- **LIFX light**: the light.
- **Color**: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink or white
  (white bulbs pulse in white).
- **Pulse**: **Blink** (on and off) or **Breathe** (smooth).
- **Length of one cycle**: 0.25 to 5 seconds.
- **Number of cycles (1-50)**: 3 by default.

Output: **Duration of the pulse (s)**, to wait for its end in the scene.

### Start a LIFX effect

Turns the light on and starts a built-in effect, which runs until stopped
(another effect, a color, a white, or **Stop the effect**).

- **Effect**: **Move (strips)**, **Morph (matrices)**, **Flame (matrices)** or
  **Stop the effect**.
- **Speed**: slow, normal or fast.
- **Direction (Move)**: right or left.
- **Colors**: rainbow, fire, ocean, forest, pastel, or **Colors already shown
  (Move)**. Move paints them along the strip before sliding them; Morph blends
  them; Flame keeps its own colors.

Output: **Effect running (move, morph, flame, none)**.

## Why no widget

The Gladys light box already shows and controls everything a LIFX light does:
on/off, brightness, color, white, infrared and the effect list. The pulse and
the effects with their settings are scene actions, where they are useful
(alerts, ambiances). A LIFX widget would only repeat the light box, so there is
none.

## Scene examples

- **Door left open**: when the door sensor stays open 5 minutes → **Pulse a
  LIFX light**, the living room light, orange, Blink, 1 second, 5 cycles.
- **Doorbell**: when the doorbell rings → **Pulse a LIFX light**, the office
  light, blue, Breathe, 0.5 seconds, 6 cycles (one action per light to warn).
- **Movie night**: at 9 pm, when the TV turns on → **Start a LIFX effect**,
  the TV strip, Move, slow, ocean; and **Stop the effect** when it turns off.
- **Light switched off at the wall**: when **Connection** of a light goes to 0
  for 10 minutes → send a message "the hall light is unpowered".

## Network traffic and limits of the protocol

- The LIFX protocol has no push: each light added to Gladys is read at the
  refresh interval (one or two small UDP packets, three for a strip or a
  matrix). LIFX asks clients to stay under 20 messages per second per light:
  the integration sends one message at a time per light, far below.
- Gladys only receives the values that changed, plus the unchanged ones every
  6 hours so that the history stays fresh.
- The lights are searched again every 15 minutes, to follow their address
  changes and find new ones.
- The integration reads the lights with its own timer: Gladys does not poll
  them (the devices are published with `should_poll: false`).

## Troubleshooting

- **No light found**: check that the lights are set up in the LIFX app and on
  the same network as Gladys. Automatic discovery goes through Gladys (Gladys
  5.1 or later); on another network, enter the IP addresses.
- **A light is "unreachable"**: it is switched off at the wall, or its address
  changed. The integration finds it again by itself at the next search; give
  it a fixed address in your router to avoid it.
- **The changes made in the LIFX app show late**: they show at the next read;
  choose a shorter refresh interval.
- **An effect does nothing**: Move only exists on strips, Morph and Flame on
  matrices. Move with **Colors already shown (Move)** on a strip of one color
  shows no movement: choose a palette.
- **Logs**: the integration logs only what matters (start, lights found, lost
  and back, errors). For the details, set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the container.

## Limitations

- Developed without the hardware: the behavior on real LIFX lights is still to
  be confirmed.
- Strips and matrices are controlled as a whole: no color per zone.
- The color shown for a strip or a matrix is the one the light reports for the
  whole device (its first zone).
- Not handled: the LIFX Switch (relays and buttons), the HEV cleaning cycle of
  the LIFX Clean bulbs (the bulb itself works as a color light), the Sky and
  Color sweep effects (shown as **Other effect**), the LIFX cloud and scenes of
  the LIFX app.
- A product newer than the product list of the integration is handled as a
  color light with a 1500-9000 K white range, until an update.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings LIFX asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Finding your LIFX lights | `section` | No | LIFX lights on the same network as Gladys are found automatically: open the Discovery tab. Set them up in the LIFX app first. If one is missing, enter its IP address below. |
| IP addresses of LIFX lights | `string` | No | Optional, separated by commas. Only needed for the lights automatic discovery does not find. |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often each light is read, to follow the changes made from the LIFX app, a voice assistant or a wall switch. |
| Transition | `select` | No | Fade of the changes made from Gladys: on, off, brightness, color and white. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Names given to the features of new lights (Light, Brightness, LIFX effect...). The light names come from the LIFX app. |

## How to install LIFX in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: LIFX appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-lifx:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-lifx](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-lifx).

LIFX requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
